message: We need a restaurant system that can handle sales, staff, and daily operations without everything becoming chaotic during service.
Who are the different users or roles that will use this system?

We’ve got cashiers handling the register, floor staff taking orders, shift managers keeping an eye on things, and then myself and my partner running the overall business. Right now, it's too easy for people to step on each other's toes or make changes they shouldn't, so I need everyone locked into their own specific roles.
Do you operate from a single location or multiple locations or branches?

We currently have two locations running, and we're looking to open a third later this year. Right now, keeping tabs on sales, inventory, and staff across locations without physically being there all day is becoming a real headache.
How do you currently track your inventory, records, or data, and what problems come up?

Right now it's a total mess of spreadsheets and manual counts at the end of the week, which means we're constantly finding out about missing stock or pricing mistakes way too late. It takes hours to piece together what actually sold across both sites, and I never really know if the numbers are accurate until it's already hurting our margins.
Walk me through what happens in your core daily workflow from start to finish.

Well, it usually starts first thing in the morning when the managers open up, check the overnight deliveries, and make sure the registers have the right float. Once the doors open, it’s straight into a rush with front-of-house taking orders, kitchen firing tickets, and cashiers handling payments right through the midday peak. In the afternoon things slow down a bit for prep, but then we hit the evening dinner rush all over again. At the end of the night, the managers have to count down the drawers, try to match cash and card totals to what was actually sold, and figure out why the numbers never quite seem to line up.
How do payments or transactions get handled and reconciled today?

Right now, cashiers take payments at the register using a mix of cash, cards, and sometimes digital wallets, while floor staff might also take payments on mobile devices when it gets busy. At the end of every shift, the manager has to pull the Z-reports, count the physical cash in the drawer by hand, and try to match it against the credit card batch totals and what the system says was sold. It takes forever, and honestly, if there's a discrepancy, it's almost impossible to figure out who made the mistake or where the money went.
What reporting or visibility do you need across the business?

I need to be able to see real-time sales and cash drawer totals for both locations from my phone without having to call the manager every hour. At the end of the day, I want a clean breakdown of what actually sold, who handled what, and where any shortages happened so I can spot problems before they eat into our margins.
What other tools or systems does this need to work with?

Right now we just use some basic card processing terminals and a separate accounting tool that our bookkeeper uses. Whatever we bring in needs to connect cleanly with our payment terminals so staff aren't manually typing in amounts, and it has to export data into our accounting software without a huge hassle.
